Author: Anil Kumar Sinha

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Petitioner/s
 Versus
 1. The State Of Bihar
 2. Gajala Praveen Daughter of Md. Abul Hassan Resident of Village-
 Niyamatpur, P.S. Barsoi, District- Katihar.

Respondent/s
 ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Bimal Kumar
 For the Respondent/s : Mr. Anuj Kumar Shrivastava
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Anil Kumar Sinha
 Oral Order
5 17-07-2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties concerned.

The present revision application has been directed against the judgment and order dated 08.08.2019 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-III, Katihar in Criminal Appeal No. 46 of 2012 by which the judgment and order dated 08.05.2012 passed by the learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Katihar in G.R. No. 1642 of 2006/TR No. 1251 of 2012 (arising out of Barsoi (Sudhani OP) PS Case No. 99 of 2006, dated 19.11.2006, by which the petitioner has been convicted under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced him to undergo imprisonment of two years and a fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default of payment of fine he may further go imprisonment for two months.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Patna High Court CR. REV. No.1190 of 2019(5)
dt.17-07-2023 petitioner is husband of the informant and his marriage was solemnized with the informant on 01.03.2006.

He further submits that the allegation against the petitioner is of demand of dowry of Rs. 50,000/- and due to non-fulfillment of demand, the petitioner and his family members have tortured the informant, physically and mentally.
He next submits that during the course of trial, altogether six witnesses were examined by the prosecution, but all are related witnesses and are family members of the informant itself.
Whereas, the allegation is that the petitioner tortured the informant for non-fulfillment of demand of dowry at the matrimonial home of the informant.

None of the witnesses from matrimonial home has been examined by the Md. Sabul Hussain vs The State Of Bihar on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148188610/
1 prosecution.

entities.text: Md. Sabul Hussain vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He next submits that during the course of trial, the petitioner was on bail and after conviction, by the Trial Court on 08.05.2012, the petitioner was granted bail by the Trial Court on the same day.

The petitioner preferred appeal before the learned lower Appellate Court, whereas,
appeal was dismissed on 08.08.2019.
The petitioner has surrendered before the District Court on 20.03.2013, since then he is in custody.

Taking into consideration the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner and the fact that all along during the Patna High Court CR. REV. No.1190 of 2019(5) dt.17-07-2023 course of trial the petitioner remained on bail and nature of evidence adduced, I am inclined to grant the petitioner privilege of bail till final disposal of this revision application.

Let the petitioner, above named, be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount, each to the satisfaction of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Katiha in connection to the G.R. No. 1642 of 2006/TR No. 1251 of 2012 (arising out of Barsoi (Sudhani OP) PS Case No. 99 of 2006.

Issue notice to the opposite party no. 2, in the hearing matter, for which, requisites etc., under both process i.e., ordinary as well as by registered cover/speed post with A/D, must be filed within two weeks, failing which this application shall stand rejected without further reference to a Bench.
Rule is made returnable within six months.

(Anil Kumar Sinha, J) ashwani/-
